abstract.text: We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate effective Hamiltonian.

thesis.text: In the Minkowskian non-Abelian Higgs model with vacuum BPS monopoles, the BPS ansatzes act as electric form-factors, implying soft CP-invariance violation analogous to the instanton theta-term.

sections.summary: To investigate the singular behavior of the local energy for the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole solutions near the poles, we consider the approximated metric near the poles, and match it with the near-horizon form of the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole. The result is that there is a \(C^{0}\) singularity at the poles. It is argued that the singularity is very weak and that the corresponding geodesics are C1. In particular, the tidal forces are finite. It is further commented that the singularity disappears in the extremal limit.
sections.title: Singularity of the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole near the poles

sections.summary: The new form of the metric near the poles is consistent with the previous results of the energy-momentum tensor for the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole. This gives further evidence that the equations of motion are satisfied near the poles.
sections.title: Consistency with the energy-momentum tensor near the poles

abstract.text: We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate effective Hamiltonian.

thesis.text: In the Minkowskian non-Abelian Higgs model with vacuum BPS monopoles, the BPS ansatzes act as electric form-factors, implying soft CP-invariance violation analogous to the instanton theta-term.

sections.summary: To investigate the singular behavior of the local energy for the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole solutions near the poles, we consider the approximated metric near the poles, and match it with the near-horizon form of the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole. The result is that there is a \(C^{0}\) singularity at the poles. It is argued that the singularity is very weak and that the corresponding geodesics are C1. In particular, the tidal forces are finite. It is further commented that the singularity disappears in the extremal limit.
sections.title: Singularity of the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole near the poles

sections.summary: The new form of the metric near the poles is consistent with the previous results of the energy-momentum tensor for the Kerr-Newman-dS black hole. This gives further evidence that the equations of motion are satisfied near the poles.
sections.title: Consistency with the energy-momentum tensor near the poles

sections.summary: The Dirac fundamental quantization of the YMH model with vacuum BPS monopoles refines the CP-violation discussion. Zero modes Z^a to the YM Gauss law constraint yield vacuum electric monopoles and an action W_N = ∫ dt (I/2) Ndot^2, with rotary momentum I=4π^2/(α_s V <B^2>) and P_N = Ndot I = 2πk+θ. Unlike the instanton θ-vacuum, this action is manifestly P- and C-invariant, even in total electric charge Q=Σ q_i of Higgs vacuum BPS monopole modes, so the model conserves CP in this respect.
